checks: Isolating each exposed binary base gives the ordinary ball depth exactly. Its centroid has raw depth V/2, which is the mixed maximum.

The four edge midpoints belong to the ambient level by opposite-pair symmetry. Convexity and continuous reflection reduce projection exclusion to a point with continuous coordinate zero. The affine Hamming-distance cut outside the diamond has threshold greater than -1 at its one nearest binary vertex and at least 1 at each other vertex, so the cap has mass below V.

At a three-base barycenter, any two thresholds with nonpositive sum already pay V by the symmetric ball-tail identity. Otherwise each threshold is smaller than the total and all three tails pay more than V for a sufficiently small continuous ball there. Together with the edge midpoints this gives full dimension. The open split has no lattice point, and an added exterior point puts a boundary lattice point in the interior of the convex enlargement.

In rank one the two opposite continuous margins balance to -2M z_2 and can be made equal on each base plane. Their proper inward shifts take less than V from the formerly whole captured ball and keep all other traces empty in volume, proving actual support.

For the rank-d group the coordinate normals and their negative sum have exactly one positive relation. The last bottom trace is strictly full at its own site and strictly empty on the other because d exceeds √d. The first d traces have at most tangent sections on the bottom pair. M≥4d+4 excludes every top site.

The inequalities from the diamond and the two-bottom-half test caps bound every rank-d margin by zero on the entire level set, even when an individual rank-d cap initially has strict full/empty margins. Setting x_k=2(z_1-1/2) for each k checks the converse in the whole-plane coverage calculation.

After reflection the two groups cover all four positive fibers. A vertical halfspace preserving either group's sampled coverage contains two full fibers and has mass at least 2V. The proposed two-group budget 2V cannot bound their total mass 4V.

overlap.comparison: The accepted tiny-extra-fiber example proves actual null sections at a different exposed depth facet and calculates an intersection projection. The present square-ball split constructs reflected groups whose unions cover exact base exteriors and disproves a coverage-preserving vertical replacement and the resulting total budget.

readability: The exact projected exteriors describe whole-plane coverage by the union. They are separate from the projected depth region and from projection of the intersection of the caps.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The square-ball example has the claimed ambient depth region, supporting null-section circuits of both ranks, and a strict mass obstruction to coverage-preserving vertical replacement.
